draft.title: How markets answer the economic questions
card: Every economy must decide what to produce, how to produce it and who gets it. This is because resources are limited and wants are not.
In a market economy, buyers and sellers trading freely make these decisions. No single person or group plans the whole thing.
What
businesses make the goods and services that buyers are willing to pay for. If buyers want more of something, prices and profits can rise, and businesses may make more of it.
How
businesses choose the methods and resources to use, often looking for ways to keep costs low. Who gets the goods: people who are willing and able to pay the price.
draft.remember: In a market economy, free trade between buyers and sellers answers what, how and who.

a.q: In a market economy, what mainly decides which goods and services get made?
opts: What buyers are willing to pay for
What workers vote to make each year
a.why: Businesses make what buyers will pay for, because that is how they earn profit. A planning office deciding is not how a market economy works, as buyers and sellers trading freely make the choices.
a.clue: Think about who spends money and who wants a profit.

b.q: Jaya runs a bakery in Hobart. More people start buying sourdough, so she bakes more of it and less white bread. Which question does this answer?
b.why: Jaya changes which goods she makes because of what buyers want, so this answers what to produce. It is not how to produce, because her methods and resources have not changed.
b.clue: She changed the product, not the method or the buyer.

a.best: What buyers are willing to pay for

problems.detail: 'Free trade' is an established economic term for trade between countries without tariffs or barriers. The card says 'trading freely', and the remember line should match that wording to avoid confusion.

The why says Jaya's 'methods and resources have not changed', but the scenario never says so, and sourdough uses different ingredients and a different process from white bread. The why should just say the decision is about which goods she makes.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer that matches the card. There are two minor fixes: the remember line says 'free trade' (a term with another meaning) where the card says 'trading freely', and why (b) claims Jaya's resources are unchanged, which the scenario never says.
